cards.headline: Posters across LA, then a leak forced an early release
cards.snippet: In February 2017, Lana Del Rey began teasing "Love," the lead single from her album Lust for Life, with promotional posters hung around Los Angeles on February 17. That same day, leaked versions of the song surfaced online. Because of the leaks, the release date was moved up, and the song came out on February 18, 2017. It was her first new music in nearly 16 months.
cards.context: Lead single from Lust for Life, her first release in nearly 16 months.

cards.headline: The song ends with a nod to the Beach Boys
cards.snippet: Lana Del Rey's 2017 single "Love" closes with a nod to the Beach Boys' classic "Don't Worry Baby." Rolling Stone described the track as retro-sounding and inspired by Sixties girl groups, and the ending fits that feel. The song's original title was a lyric, "Oh, to be young and in love."
cards.context: Rolling Stone described the track as retro-sounding and Sixties girl group-inspired.

cards.headline: Lana teases the kids streaming old songs on new tech
cards.snippet: Per the Genius annotation, Lana points to the irony of young listeners finding old music through satellite radio and streaming, which didn't exist when it was made. It also hints at nostalgia clashing with a hi-tech world.
cards.context: One 2,300-like comment spots the joke: "Lana: Makes vintage and very aesthetic music Also Lana: Look at you kids with your vintage music."

lyric.excerptOrTimestamp: Look at you, kids, with your vintage music
lyric.selectionNote: Quoted in 7 of the top 300 YouTube comments on the song's uploads (6.8K likes between them); also the song's most-voted annotation on Genius (245 votes).
